title: Room booking schema in PostgreSQL
idea: The schema stores each booking's time as a `tstzrange`, and an exclusion constraint makes PostgreSQL itself refuse two active bookings of one room that overlap.

analogy.text: A wall planner where each booking is a strip of tape. The planner physically refuses a strip that would cover another strip in the same row.
analogy.breaks: Cancelled strips stay on the wall but stop blocking.

points: `during` is a half-open `tstzrange`; a CHECK forbids empty, closed or unbounded ranges.
The restaurant's exclusion constraint again, now per room: `=` on room, `&&` on time.
Its GiST index can also serve the free-room query for a window.
`booking_organizer_idx` serves the my-meetings screen for one employee.

hero.title: The no-overlap constraint, part by part

parts.label: Constraint kind
parts.note: An exclusion constraint refuses a row that conflicts with any existing row, using a GiST index.

parts.label: Same room
parts.note: Rows conflict only when room_id is equal. Using = in GiST needs the btree_gist extension.

parts.label: Overlapping time
parts.note: && is true when two ranges share any instant. Half-open ranges let 11:00 follow 11:00.

parts.label: Active only
parts.note: Cancelled, completed and released rows are ignored, so they never block a new booking.

code.title: Tables and constraints
code.caption: The schema on a real PostgreSQL 18, then eight writes: the database refuses four of them by itself.

walk.text: Enable btree_gist; employee and room tables with UNIQUE email and a capacity CHECK.
Foreign keys to room and employee; `during` must be a bounded, non-empty [start, end) range.
Status is TEXT with a CHECK; `version` supports optimistic locking on edits.
No overlap among active bookings per room; an index for each organizer's meetings.
Insert via `tstzrange`, printing error codes; reversed times fail there with 22000, before any CHECK.
Overlap, back-to-back, other room, cancelled overlap, reversed times, bad room, bad status.
Free rooms for four: big enough, and no active booking overlapping the window.

code.title: Two clients at once
code.caption: Two transactions insert overlapping bookings in parallel; then two editors move one booking with optimistic locking.

walk.text: Each attempt uses its own client and transaction, and returns ok or the error code.
Both run in parallel. Sorting hides who won; only the outcome counts.
Count the rows: the constraint decided, not the timing.
Each editor updates only if `version` is still 0, and bumps it.
The second update re-checks `version` after the first commits and matches no row.

pitfalls: Do not store start and end without a constraint; app checks alone race across servers.
Forgetting the WHERE clause makes cancelled bookings block the room forever.
Use `[)` ranges; inclusive ends make back-to-back meetings clash.

quiz.q: Which error code does BK-2 print in schema.mjs?
quiz.why: BK-2 overlaps BK-1 in R-1 while both are BOOKED. The exclusion constraint refuses it with exclusion violation 23P01.

takeaway: Let an exclusion constraint guarantee no overlapping active bookings per room.
